items.title: Bedford County Senior Property Tax Freeze
items.summary: Freezes the county property tax dollar amount for qualifying homeowners age 65 and older whose household income is at or under $43,780.
items.bedfordImpact: The Commission votes Tuesday, December 8, 2026, at 7:00 PM at the Historic Courthouse. If approved, the county must file its resolution with the Tennessee Comptroller by December 31, 2026. The freeze holds a qualifying owner's tax bill flat against future reappraisals or rate hikes. Owners must reapply each year at the Trustee's office by early April.
actionSteps: Track the December 8, 2026 commission vote at the Historic Courthouse.
If passed, submit county certification paperwork to the Tennessee Comptroller before December 31, 2026.
Prepare Trustee appointment intake (931-684-4303) for the spring application window.

sources.label: Bedford County News: Senior Tax Freeze Goes to Commission Dec 8

items.title: County & School Budget Amendments and Solid Waste Authority Review
items.summary: Sends mid-year county and school budget amendments to the full Commission and flags discussions with Shelbyville on leaving the interlocal solid waste authority.
items.bedfordImpact: On November 24, 2026, the Financial Management Committee advanced both a school budget amendment and a county budget amendment to the December 8 commission agenda. Officials also reported that Shelbyville and Bedford County are evaluating an exit from the interlocal solid waste authority, which would reshape county solid waste operations and costs.
actionSteps: Review final amendment amounts ahead of the December 8, 2026 commission meeting.
Track any interlocal solid waste exit study or resolution at the December 15 Financial Management Committee meeting.

items.title: Ending the Grocery Tax by Closing Corporate Loopholes Act
items.summary: Pre-filed bill for the 2027 session that proposes eliminating Tennessee's grocery tax and offsetting the revenue through corporate tax changes.
items.bedfordImpact: Not signed into law yet. Any state legislation altering food sales taxes matters directly to Bedford County because local option sales tax is a major funding stream for Bedford County Schools and the county general fund. Finance staff should watch whether amendments touch only the state 4 percent food rate or also affect local option collections.
actionSteps: Watch for the Fiscal Review fiscal note once the 115th General Assembly opens January 12, 2027.
Verify whether local option sales tax collections for Bedford County and Bedford County Schools stay untouched.
items.statute: Proposed amendment to T.C.A. Title 57 and Title 67

items.title: State Sales Tax Repeal on Fresh Produce, Meat, Dairy, Eggs & Bread
items.summary: Pre-filed bill eliminating the state sales tax on fresh or frozen produce, poultry, fish, lean raw meat, eggs, dairy, whole grains, legumes, and bread.
items.bedfordImpact: Submitted by neighboring District 92 Rep. Todd Warner ahead of the 2027 session. As drafted, it targets the state sales tax rate rather than local sales tax, but county finance leaders should track committee amendments and any indirect changes to state shared sales-tax distributions to counties.
actionSteps: Monitor House Finance subcommittee assignment after January 12, 2027.
Check Fiscal Review estimates for any impact on county state-shared revenue.
items.statute: Proposed amendment to T.C.A. Title 67, Chapter 6

items.title: Sales Tax Holiday Computer Exemption Increase ($1,500 to $2,500)
items.summary: Pre-filed bill raising the tax-free price cap on computers during Tennessee's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday from $1,500 to $2,500.
items.bedfordImpact: Not yet enacted. Expanding the sales tax holiday exemption helps Bedford County families buying laptops, while slightly trimming local option sales tax receipts during holiday weekend unless the state reimburses local governments.
actionSteps: Watch whether the 2027 state budget includes local government hold-harmless reimbursement if HB 0007 advances.
items.statute: Proposed amendment to T.C.A. Title 67, Chapter 6

items.citation: HB 0005 & HB 0012 (115th General Assembly, Pre-Filed Nov 2026)
items.title: Property Assessment & Tax Relief Electronic Reporting Bills (Caption Vehicles)
items.body: Tennessee 115th General Assembly (Rep. Jason Zachary & House Sponsors)
items.summary: Early pre-filed property-tax bills updating electronic Comptroller reporting for the property tax relief program and Division of Property Assessments.
items.bedfordImpact: In Tennessee, narrow early-filed bills amending T.C.A. Title 67, Chapter 5 often serve as caption bills that get amended in spring with broader property tax relief or reappraisal rules. Bedford County's Property Assessor and Trustee should watch both bills for late amendments affecting senior tax relief thresholds or county reappraisal rules.
actionSteps: Keep HB 0005 and HB 0012 on the county watchlist for committee amendments once the 115th General Assembly begins.
items.statute: Proposed amendments to T.C.A. Title 67, Chapter 5

items.title: FY 2026-27 County Budget ($198.2M) & Certified Property Tax Rate ($1.5083)
items.summary: Sets Bedford County's $198,205,381 budget for FY 2026-27 and adopts the state-certified revenue-neutral property tax rate of $1.5083 per $100 assessed value after the 2026 reappraisal.
items.bedfordImpact: Approved June 30, 2026. Major funds include General Purpose Schools ($106.88M), County General Fund ($43.64M), Debt Service ($22.22M), Child Nutrition ($8.43M), Education Capital Projects ($6.59M), Highway/Public Works ($5.06M), and County Capital Projects ($4.72M). Tax rate breakdown: $0.9276 General, $0.4022 Schools, $0.0973 Debt Service, $0.0584 Highway, and $0.0228 Capital Projects.
actionSteps: Monitor quarterly department spending against FY 2026-27 line items before the June 30, 2027 fiscal year close.

sources.label: Bedford County Official Notice: Commission Approves FY 2026-27 Budget & Tax Rate

items.title: Voters Approve State Property Tax Ban, Expanded Bail Denial & Victims' Rights
items.summary: Tennessee voters passed all three statewide constitutional amendments on November 3, 2026, each clearing both a majority of votes on the measure and a majority of votes cast for Governor.
items.bedfordImpact: Amendment 2 (66.7 percent Yes) permanently bans the state legislature from levying a state property tax, preserving property tax solely for counties and cities like Bedford County. Amendment 1 (67.1 percent Yes) expands offenses eligible for pretrial denial of bail, which can raise county jail populations and court hearings. Amendment 3 (76.1 percent Yes) adds constitutional notice and safety rights for crime victims.
actionSteps: Watch county jail pretrial housing counts as courts apply Amendment 1 bail rules.
Confirm court clerk and victim-notice procedures align with Amendment 3.
items.statute: Tennessee Constitution Art. I Sec. 15, Art. I Sec. 35, Art. II Sec. 28

sources.label: Tennessee Secretary of State: 2026 Proposed Amendments
Tennessee Firefly: Nov 2026 General Election Results

items.title: County Zoning Resolution Overhaul & Combined Codes Inspector Role
items.summary: Updates Bedford County's zoning resolution to place a zoning officer inside the Codes Department and clean up outdated language.
items.bedfordImpact: Sent to the December 8, 2026 commission agenda by the Rules and Legislative Committee. County Mayor Curt Cobb said the change lets inspectors cover both building and zoning work from one office, speeding up permitting ahead of state review deadlines taking effect January 1, 2027.
actionSteps: Follow the December 8, 2026 commission vote on the revised zoning text.
Align updated Codes and Zoning workflows with Tennessee Public Chapter 1044 review timelines starting January 1, 2027.

items.title: Mandatory Development Review Timelines & Surety Release Rules
items.summary: Sets state deadlines for county review of development applications, site plans, inspections, written deficiency notices, and engineer-certified surety releases.
items.bedfordImpact: Takes effect January 1, 2027. Bedford County planning and codes staff must track statutory review clocks and limits on written deficiency letters. The law also creates a formal path for developers to use a licensed engineer to certify contract completion and seek release of subdivision performance bonds.
actionSteps: Set up application date-stamp tracking in Codes and Planning before January 1, 2027.
Review subdivision bond release language with the County Attorney and Highway Department.

items.title: Endocrine-Disrupting Pharmaceuticals Water Safety Act
items.summary: Pre-filed 2027 bill directing TDEC to list endocrine-disrupting pharmaceuticals of concern and imposing new water and wastewater monitoring or treatment requirements.
items.bedfordImpact: Not signed into law yet. If enacted, new state water-quality monitoring and treatment mandates would directly affect public water and wastewater plants drawing from and discharging into the Duck River, including Bedford County Utility District and Shelbyville Power, Water, and Sewerage System.
actionSteps: Alert local utility directors to review the full text of HB 0002 before committee hearings begin in January 2027.
Watch Fiscal Review estimates for local water and sewer compliance costs.
items.statute: Proposed amendment to T.C.A. Title 4 and Title 68

items.title: One-Year Moratorium on Large and Hyperscale Data Centers
items.summary: Pauses all permits and zoning approvals for large-scale (40 MW+) and hyperscale (101 MW+) data centers in unincorporated Bedford County for one year.
items.bedfordImpact: Passed unanimously August 11, 2026. The resolution cites heavy water demand (1 to 5 million gallons daily), Duck River Watershed protection, noise, and power grid limits. The county now has until August 11, 2027 to draft permanent zoning, noise, water-reuse, and lighting standards.
actionSteps: Complete technical zoning, water, and noise standards before the moratorium expires August 11, 2027.
Pair local standards with Tennessee Public Chapter 961, which bars utilities from absorbing data center electric infrastructure costs.

items.title: County Authority to End Municipal Extraterritorial Zoning
items.summary: Authorizes counties under 341,500 population to vote by majority to stop municipalities from exercising zoning authority outside city limits.
items.bedfordImpact: Bedford County (population 55,273) qualifies. If the County Commission opts in, anyone filing a plat, site plan, or building permit inside an urban growth boundary outside city limits must record an annexation declaration with the Register of Deeds. City zoning standards apply only if the owner seeks annexation.
actionSteps: Review whether Bedford County wants to opt in by majority Commission resolution.
Coordinate with the Register of Deeds on recording annexation declarations if adopted.

items.title: Federal Highway & Bridge Reauthorization ($580B Bill / Dec 11 Deadline)
items.summary: Five-year, $580 billion highway, bridge, and rural transit bill awaiting a House floor vote while temporary federal highway authority expires December 11, 2026.
items.bedfordImpact: The 2021 infrastructure law (IIJA) expired September 30, 2026, and Division J advance funds for the Bridge Formula Program and Safe Streets for All already lapsed. H.R. 8870 passed House committee 62-2 and creates a new Surface Transportation Accelerator Grant program for rural and local roads, adds an annual federal EV fee ($130 EV / $35 plug-in hybrid), and funds highway safety and bridge grants through FY 2031.
actionSteps: Monitor Congress before December 11, 2026 for a multi-year highway bill or another extension.
Track restoration of Bridge Formula and rural road safety grants for Bedford County Highway Department.
Watch the CR's OMB Uniform Guidance delay if managing active federal grants.

items.title: 2026 Federal Farm Bill Reauthorization (Rural Facilities, Water & Broadband)
items.summary: Five-year reauthorization of USDA rural development, Community Facilities grants, rural water and broadband funding, conservation, and SNAP through FY 2031.
items.bedfordImpact: Passed the House 224-200 on April 30, 2026 and cleared Senate Agriculture Committee on September 16, 2026, awaiting a Senate floor vote. USDA Community Facilities grants help rural counties like Bedford fund public buildings, vehicles, and water systems. NACo backs reauthorization while warning against provisions preempting county authority over livestock and pesticides.
actionSteps: Watch Senate floor action during the December 2026 lame-duck session.
Track final USDA Community Facilities and rural broadband funding rules for FY 2027.

sources.label: Congress.gov: H.R. 7567 Farm, Food, and National Security Act

items.title: Rural Partnership and Prosperity Act
items.summary: Creates multi-year (2 to 5 year) flexible USDA Rural Partnership grants and technical assistance grants for counties, cities, nonprofits, and regional partners.
items.bedfordImpact: Not signed into law yet, and supported by NACo for inclusion in the Farm Bill. Unlike narrow capital-only grants, these awards could fund county predevelopment planning, grant-writing and project staffing, public-private partnerships, and disaster economic recovery in rural counties like Bedford.
actionSteps: Watch whether H.R. 6041 language is folded into the final Farm Bill or re-filed in the 120th Congress.

sources.label: Congress.gov: H.R. 6041 Rural Partnership and Prosperity Act

items.title: $10 Million Highway 231 Sewer Expansion Grant Transfer
items.summary: Transfers $10,000,000 in state infrastructure grant funds from Bedford County to Shelbyville Power, Water, and Sewerage System for Highway 231 sewer expansion.
items.bedfordImpact: Adopted August 11, 2026. Shelbyville Power, Water, and Sewerage System handles procurement, construction, ownership, and upkeep of the new wastewater lines along the Highway 231 growth corridor, and uses the $10 million state grant as local match for a U.S. EDA Public Works federal grant.
actionSteps: Track interlocal transfer milestones and EDA Public Works grant award updates.

items.title: Paramedic Determination and Pronouncement of Death
items.summary: Authorizes licensed Tennessee paramedics to determine and pronounce death outside a hospital after resuscitation attempts if they complete EMS Board training.
items.bedfordImpact: Takes effect January 1, 2027. Bedford County EMS paramedics who intend to pronounce death in the field must finish the state-approved course first and keep proof of completion ready for EMS Board inspection. Does not apply inside a hospital. Non-compliance can trigger EMS Board discipline.
actionSteps: Verify state EMS Board training course completion for every participating BCEMS paramedic before January 1, 2027.
File certificates in personnel training records so proof is available on request.
Update county EMS field termination and Medical Examiner notification protocols.
items.statute: T.C.A. Title 68, Chapter 3, Part 5 and Chapter 140, Part 3

items.citation: P.L. 119-75 Sec. 6203 & CMS CY 2027 PFS Final Rule
items.title: Medicare Rural Ambulance Add-Ons & New CY 2027 Rural ZIP Rules
items.keyDateLabel: New CMS RUCA ZIP map takes effect
items.summary: Extends the 3 percent rural and 22.6 percent super-rural Medicare ambulance add-ons through December 31, 2027, while updating rural ZIP boundaries on January 1, 2027.
items.bedfordImpact: Good revenue news and an immediate billing check. Congress locked in Medicare rural ambulance add-ons through 2027 under the Consolidated Appropriations Act (P.L. 119-75). Starting January 1, 2027, CMS switches to OMB Bulletin 23-01 and RUCA 4.0+ codes to define rural pickup ZIP codes. Billing software must load the CY 2027 CMS ZIP file so Bedford County calls bill at the right rural rate.
actionSteps: Check every Bedford County pickup ZIP code in the CMS CY 2027 PFS ZIP table for urban, rural, or super-rural changes.
Confirm EMS billing software updates the Ambulance Fee Schedule effective January 1, 2027.
Plan ahead for the next federal Medicare add-on expiration on December 31, 2027.

sources.label: CMS Ambulance News & CY 2027 Final Rule
EMS1: Congress Extends Medicare Ambulance Add-Ons Through 2027

items.title: Fixing Emergency Management for Americans (FEMA) Act
items.summary: Bipartisan bill passed 57-3 by the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee to make FEMA an independent cabinet agency and overhaul disaster grants.
items.bedfordImpact: Not signed into law yet. Directly affects how Bedford County gets reimbursed after tornadoes, floods, and severe storms. Adds expedited facility repair grants, optional block grants for smaller disasters, and noncompetitive formula mitigation grants as federal review proposals weigh shifting disaster costs toward counties.
actionSteps: Monitor House floor action and any federal Public Assistance cost-share changes.
Keep county disaster procurement and damage documentation audit-ready.

items.title: Due Process Continuity of Care Act (Medicaid for Pretrial County Jail Detainees)
items.body: 119th U.S. Congress (Sen. Bill Cassidy, Senate Finance)
items.summary: Allows states to keep Medicaid benefits active for eligible pretrial detainees held in county jails while awaiting trial before any conviction.
items.bedfordImpact: Not signed into law yet, and a top NACo county priority. Under current federal Medicaid rules, Bedford County taxpayers absorb nearly all medical, mental health, and hospital bills for inmates who have not been convicted. Passing this bill would cut county jail healthcare costs and keep mental health medications uninterrupted.
actionSteps: Track Senate Finance action or reintroduction in the 120th Congress.
Coordinate with the Sheriff's Office on annual pretrial jail medical cost figures if briefing federal lawmakers.

sources.label: Congress.gov: S. 1720 Due Process Continuity of Care Act

items.title: BEAD Funds for County Tornado Sirens & Disaster Warning Sensors
items.body: 119th U.S. Congress (Sen. John Cornyn, Senate Commerce)
items.summary: Lets states use leftover federal BEAD broadband funds for competitive subgrants to counties for warning sirens, flood and wind sensors, and alert systems.
items.bedfordImpact: Not signed into law yet. If passed, Tennessee could subgrant leftover BEAD broadband funds to Bedford County for outdoor tornado warning sirens, Duck River flood sensors, and alert equipment (prioritizing local projects with a 25 percent local match).
actionSteps: Monitor Senate Commerce Committee progress or 120th Congress reintroduction.
Keep a list of priority tornado siren and flood-sensor gap areas ready in EMA.

items.title: Off-Duty Law Enforcement Carrying Firearms on School Grounds
items.summary: Pre-filed 2027 bill removing the requirement that an off-duty law enforcement officer carrying a firearm onto school grounds immediately notify the school principal.
items.bedfordImpact: Not signed into law yet. If passed in 2027, Bedford County Schools and the Sheriff's Office will need to update visitor sign-in and school safety procedures for off-duty officers entering school buildings during regular school hours.
actionSteps: Watch committee assignment in January 2027 and coordinate school security protocol updates if advanced.
items.statute: Proposed amendment to T.C.A. Title 39, Ch. 17, Part 13 and Title 49

items.title: Medicare 5-Year Treatment-in-Place Ground Ambulance Test
items.body: 119th U.S. Congress (Sen. Susan Collins / Rep. Mike Carey)
items.summary: Directs Medicare's Innovation Center (CMMI) to test a 5-year payment model paying ground ambulances when they treat a Medicare patient on scene without an ER transport.
items.bedfordImpact: Not signed into law yet. Right now Medicare pays zero when Bedford County EMS treats a patient on scene who safely avoids the ER. Under S. 3145 / H.R. 2538, payment rates would align with standard transport rates. Any bill that stalls this winter must be re-filed in the 120th Congress.
actionSteps: Track whether CARE Act language attaches to a December 2026 health package or gets re-filed in January 2027.
Brief incoming District 9 Rep.-elect Brent Taylor on rural EMS non-transport call volume.

items.title: Permanent Medicare Coverage for On-Scene EMS Care Without Transport
items.body: 119th U.S. Congress (Sen. Peter Welch, Senate Finance)
items.summary: Amends Title XVIII of the Social Security Act to establish permanent Medicare coverage for ambulance care even when the patient is not transported.
items.bedfordImpact: Not signed into law yet. Goes further than the CARE Act pilot by making on-scene Medicare EMS reimbursement permanent nationwide. Currently sitting in the Senate Finance Committee with bipartisan rural interest.
actionSteps: Monitor Senate Finance activity and 120th Congress reintroduction alongside the CARE Act.

items.title: Federal Grants for Rural Community Paramedicine & Mobile Integrated Health
items.summary: Creates a new HHS grant program funding rural and underserved EMS agencies to launch Mobile Integrated Healthcare and community paramedicine programs.
items.bedfordImpact: Not signed into law yet. If enacted in the lame-duck session or 120th Congress, this program would give rural county services like Bedford County EMS dedicated federal startup funding to reduce repeat 911 calls.
actionSteps: Watch House Energy and Commerce action and 120th Congress re-filing.

items.citation: TACIR PC 413 Recommendations & 2027 TCRS EMS Re-Filing Watch
items.title: 2027 State Watch: Recurring Ambulance Equipment Grants & Retired EMS TCRS Return-to-Work
items.summary: Tracks two expected 2027 state bills: TACIR's recommendation to make Tennessee ambulance equipment grants recurring every year, and potential re-filing of TCRS retired-EMS return-to-work after SB 513 / HB 628 died.
items.bedfordImpact: TACIR's 2026 report under Public Chapter 413 urged the General Assembly to make state ambulance equipment grants recurring like county road and emergency management grants, while rejecting mandatory city-to-county ambulance billing. Meanwhile, SB 513 / HB 628 (extending TCRS return-to-work for retired EMS staff) died April 24, 2026 and may be re-filed in January.
actionSteps: Coordinate with Rep. Pat Marsh and Sen. Shane Reeves before January 12, 2027 on recurring ambulance equipment grant funding.
Watch January 2027 filings for a new TCRS EMS return-to-work bill.
items.statute: Public Chapter 413 (2025 TACIR Report), 114th GA SB 0513 / HB 0628

TN General Assembly SB 0513 / HB 0628 History

items.title: Tennessee Ground Ambulance Service Annual Assessment Extension
items.summary: Extends the state ground ambulance provider assessment through June 30, 2027 and changes late payment penalties from $50 per day to 5 percent per month.
items.bedfordImpact: Keeps Tennessee's ground ambulance supplemental TennCare reimbursement assessment active through FY 2026-27. Bedford County EMS and Finance must pay quarterly assessment notices on time to avoid the new 5 percent monthly penalty, and watch the 2027 General Assembly for renewal before June 30, 2027.
actionSteps: Calendar all quarterly TennCare ground ambulance assessment payment dates.
Track the 2027 renewal bill before the June 30, 2027 sunset.

items.title: Class E Felony & Mandatory Sentence for Assaulting a First Responder
items.summary: Makes assault against a first responder or law enforcement officer a Class E felony carrying a mandatory $10,000 fine and a mandatory minimum 60-day jail sentence.
items.bedfordImpact: In effect since July 1, 2026. Protects Bedford County EMS crews, firefighters, and deputies on scene. Defendants are not eligible for release until they serve the full 60-day minimum. Assault against a nurse is a Class A misdemeanor with a mandatory $5,000 fine and 30-day minimum jail term.
actionSteps: Brief EMS crews and supervisors on documenting scene assaults and requesting law enforcement charges under T.C.A. 39-13-116(c)(1).

items.title: Public Safety Access to Employment Records & Mental Health Screenings
items.summary: Requires public safety employers to grant employees and job applicants full access to their employment file, including mental health screenings.
items.bedfordImpact: In effect since April 27, 2026. If Bedford County declines to hire a public safety applicant because of a mental health screening, the county must give the applicant the records and allow them to submit an alternative equivalent screening at their own cost. Failure to provide records exposes the county to a lawsuit and mandatory plaintiff attorney fees.
actionSteps: Update HR, EMS, Fire, and Sheriff hiring packets to comply with full-file access requests.
Create a written review step when an applicant submits an independent mental health evaluation.

items.title: Arrestee Medical Clearance Before County Jail Intake
items.summary: Lets a sheriff or jailer refuse or delay booking an arrestee who has obvious serious injuries or an emergency condition until the arresting agency obtains medical clearance.
items.bedfordImpact: Protects the Bedford County Jail from taking custody of unscreened medical emergencies and clarifies that the arresting agency must get treatment and provide hospital discharge paperwork before jail intake. May shift pre-booking medical transport volume for Bedford County EMS and local police.
actionSteps: Ensure Jail intake staff document the factual basis whenever an intake is delayed.
Coordinate EMS, Sheriff, and Shelbyville Police handoff protocols for medical clearances.

items.title: Temporary TennCare Benefits Bridge Program
items.summary: Pre-filed 2027 bill directing the Bureau of TennCare to create a temporary medical assistance program for individuals who do not qualify for standard TennCare or CoverKids.
items.bedfordImpact: Not signed into law yet. Any expansion of temporary state health coverage affects local uninsured rates, hospital emergency room volume, and county EMS self-pay collection rates in Bedford County.
actionSteps: Track committee referral and Fiscal Review cost projections after January 12, 2027.

items.title: Expanding Childcare in Rural America Act
items.summary: Directs USDA to prioritize rural development loans and grants that expand affordable childcare and early education in rural and farming-dependent counties.
items.bedfordImpact: Not signed into law yet, and backed by NACo for the 2026 Farm Bill. Affordable childcare is one of the biggest barriers to county workforce recruitment across schools, healthcare, and local industry in Bedford County.
actionSteps: Monitor whether H.R. 5363 is included in the final Farm Bill package or re-filed in January 2027.

sources.label: Congress.gov: H.R. 5363 Expanding Childcare in Rural America Act

items.title: $50 Billion Federal Rural Health Transformation Program
items.summary: Created a $50 billion five-year federal fund for rural healthcare transformation, with all 50 states receiving FY 2026 awards and EMS services eligible.
items.bedfordImpact: Tennessee's share of the Rural Health Transformation Program is already reaching rural EMS and healthcare operations across the state, including Bedford County's 2026 rural ambulance award. Future FY 2027 through FY 2030 state tranches will shape rural hospital, telehealth, and EMS sustainability.
actionSteps: Track Tennessee's FY 2027 Rural Health Transformation Program sub-grant announcements.
Avoid duplicating equipment already funded under the 2026 Rural Health Transformation ambulance award.

sources.label: The Paramedic Foundation: Federal EMS & Rural Health Summary

items.title: School Finance Reports, Annual EMA Training, Data Center Power Costs & Essential Housing
items.summary: Bundle of 2026 county operations laws setting August 1 school spending reports, mandatory TEMA training, utility cost rules, simplified 80+ tax relief, and essential worker housing.
items.bedfordImpact: Public Chapter 1007 requires Bedford County Schools to submit annual budget and spending reports by August 1. Public Chapter 957 requires all local EMA employees to complete annual TEMA mutual-aid training and document it in personnel files. Public Chapter 961 bars utilities from absorbing data center power costs. Public Chapter 1063 drops annual income-proof rechecks for homeowners age 80+ with five consecutive years of tax relief. Public Chapter 1101 lets counties build or lease housing for essential workers.
actionSteps: Schedule Bedford County Schools annual budget and expenditure filings before August 1 (PC 1007).
Log annual TEMA mutual-aid training certificates for all EMA personnel (PC 957).
Apply simplified 80+ tax-relief renewal rules at the Trustee Office (PC 1063).

items.title: County Commission Local Rules of Procedure Deadline
items.summary: Requires every newly elected Tennessee county commission to adopt written local rules of internal procedure by majority vote within 90 days of convening.
items.bedfordImpact: CTAS issued a statewide reminder that county legislative bodies must adopt local rules by December 1, 2026. Once adopted, any change during the term needs a two-thirds vote. Any question not covered by the county rules falls back to the latest edition of Robert's Rules of Order.
actionSteps: Confirm Bedford County Board of Commissioners has formal adopted rules on file by December 1, 2026.
Note the two-thirds vote requirement before proposing any mid-term rule changes.
Keep a copy of the latest Robert's Rules of Order on hand for procedural gaps.

sources.label: CTAS Final Reminder: December 1 Local Rules Deadline

items.title: Tennessee Certificate of Title for Vessels & Local Abandoned Vessel Program
items.summary: Pre-filed 2027 bill requiring vessel owners to obtain a TWRA certificate of title starting July 1, 2028 and creating a Local Abandoned Vessel Program.
items.bedfordImpact: Not signed into law yet. Relevant to Bedford County boat owners using Normandy Lake and the Duck River, and could give local county offices a new state framework for handling abandoned watercraft.
actionSteps: Track Senate committee referral in January 2027 for County Clerk and local waterway duties.

items.title: Prohibition on Dual Local Elected Office Holding
items.summary: Prohibits a person who holds a local elected office from holding another elected public office in Tennessee at the same time.
items.bedfordImpact: Takes effect January 1, 2027. Officials who already hold two elected offices on January 1, 2027 may keep both and run for re-election to them, but once they leave either seat they cannot hold two elected offices again. Political party state executive committee seats are exempt.
actionSteps: Share eligibility guidance with the Bedford County Election Commission ahead of future candidate filing periods.

items.title: Expanded Public Comment Rights at County & School Board Meetings
items.summary: Requires counties, cities, school boards, and local authorities to allow public comment on both agenda items and any other matter within the body's jurisdiction.
items.bedfordImpact: In effect since March 26, 2026. County Commission, committees, and the Bedford County School Board cannot limit public speakers solely to items listed on that night's agenda. Reasonable time and sign-up rules still apply.
actionSteps: Confirm County Commission and committee meeting rules reflect broader public-comment scope.

items.title: Mandatory County E-Verify & Foreign-Adversary IT Bid Certifications
items.summary: Requires counties and school districts to verify all hires in E-Verify and collect vendor certifications barring foreign-adversary IT and communications products.
items.bedfordImpact: Both laws carry steep compliance risk. Under Public Chapter 772, the state may withhold all state funding if the Attorney General finds a county or school system failed to use E-Verify and retain records. Under Public Chapter 768, every IT or communications bid must include a vendor certification barring products from designated foreign adversary companies.
actionSteps: Audit county and school HR E-Verify logs to verify records are kept for the length of employment.
Add the Public Chapter 768 foreign-adversary certification clause to all county IT, radio, camera, and software RFPs.
